title: Frequently Asked Questions
subtitle: Answering all your questions about this journey.

items.q: Does my child need a visa to visit Taiwan?
items.a: U.S. passport holders do not need a visa for stays up to 90 days. The passport must be valid for at least 6 months beyond the date of entry.

items.q: My child's passport photo no longer resembles them. Should we renew early?
items.a: Yes, if your child's appearance has changed significantly, it is highly recommended to renew the passport early, even if it has not yet expired.

items.q: Will teachers accompany students on flights?
items.a: Yes, teachers and chaperones will accompany the group throughout the entire trip.

items.q: What if my child misses the group flight?
items.a: Parents must rebook and cover any associated costs. The program staff will assist the student in rejoining the group in Taiwan.

items.q: Will students always stay together as a group?
items.a: Yes, students will move in groups under supervision. During limited free time, the buddy system applies.

items.q: What if my child gets sick or injured?
items.a: For minor issues, teachers will provide first aid. For serious conditions, the student will be taken to a hospital, accompanied by a teacher, and parents will be contacted immediately. Taiwan has excellent healthcare with English-speaking doctors.

items.q: My child has a severe allergy. Can you accommodate?
items.a: Yes, if informed in advance. Dining venues will be notified, an allergy badge may be prepared, and extra precautions will be taken.

items.q: Is Taiwan safe?
items.a: Yes, Taiwan is consistently ranked among the world's safest regions. Safety measures include a buddy system, daily roll calls, curfews, emergency cards, continuous teacher supervision, and coordination with the American Institute in Taiwan (AIT).

items.q: What if there is a natural disaster (e.g., earthquake, typhoon)?
items.a: Taiwan has excellent emergency response systems. Teachers and staff will follow safety protocols, ensure student safety, and contact parents immediately.

items.q: How can I contact my child during the trip?
items.a: The coordinator's phone number (directly dialable from the U.S.) and Taiwan emergency numbers will be provided. All hotels have Wi-Fi. Students may use international roaming or purchase a local SIM/eSIM. Daily scheduled contact times will be arranged.

items.q: Will students have access to Wi-Fi/data during the trip?
items.a: Yes, all hotels have Wi-Fi. Students may also purchase local SIM/eSIM cards for personal data use.

items.q: What is included in the program fee?
items.a: The fee includes international airfare, in-country transportation, lodging, all meals, comprehensive insurance, entrance fees, bilingual guides, preparatory materials, and souvenirs. It does not include passport fees, personal shopping, or pocket money.

items.q: What payment methods are accepted?
items.a: Zelle (no processing fee), PayPal (credit card, +7% processing fee), or wire transfer. Venmo is not accepted.

items.q: Can my child have New Taiwan Dollars (NTD) upon arrival?
items.a: Yes. KICC can assist before departure. Parents may Zelle the desired exchange amount in advance, and students will receive NTD upon arrival in Taiwan.

items.q: How much pocket money should my child bring?
items.a: Around USD $300 (in NTD 9000) is usually sufficient for snacks, small souvenirs, and personal shopping.

items.q: Who will my child room with?
items.a: Students will be assigned to rooms by gender, with 2 students per room at designated safe hotels. Teachers will be on the same floor as students.

items.q: What meals are provided?
items.a: Daily meals are included, comprising hotel breakfasts, local restaurant lunches, and specialty dinners. With advance notice, vegetarian, halal, gluten-free, and allergy-friendly diets can be accommodated.

items.q: What should my child pack?
items.a: March temperatures in Taiwan typically range from 13–23 °C (55–73 °F). Students should bring layered clothing, a jacket, rain gear, comfortable walking shoes, one semi-formal outfit (for banquets or special events), and personal medications.

items.q: Is there a dress code?
items.a: Yes, students are required to dress modestly and respectfully when visiting temples and schools.

items.q: What is the luggage allowance?
items.a: Students should follow airline regulations: usually 1 checked bag (23 kg / 50 lbs) and 1 carry-on.

items.q: Can students bring laptops or iPads?
items.a: Yes, but they are responsible for their own belongings. Teachers will guide responsible use.

items.q: Do we need an adapter for electronics?
items.a: Taiwan uses Type A/B plugs (same as the U.S.), 110V voltage. No adapter is needed for U.S. devices.

items.q: What kind of volunteer work will students do?
items.a: Students may engage in community service such as assisting at schools, cultural centers, or environmental projects. Details will be confirmed before departure.

items.q: Will students have free time?
items.a: Yes, students will have limited supervised free time, such as after dinner, during market visits, and optional activities.

items.q: Are there shopping opportunities?
items.a: Yes, the itinerary includes several shopping opportunities at places such as Dihua Street, Global Mall, SOGO Department Store, night markets, and creative districts.

items.q: Are there academic tasks?
items.a: Yes, experiential academic tasks are included, such as daily reflection journals, cultural challenge tasks, and nightly group discussions.

items.q: How are language barriers addressed?
items.a: The trip includes bilingual guides, assistance from local Taiwanese student buddies, access to translation apps, and visual aids.

items.q: Is travel insurance required?
items.a: Yes, comprehensive international travel insurance is included. It covers emergency medical expenses (up to USD $100,000), lost or delayed baggage, trip delays or interruptions, and 24/7 emergency assistance.

items.q: How do you handle homesickness or culture shock?
items.a: Teachers will provide regular check-ins and support, group reflection sessions, peer buddy support, and, if necessary, brief contact with family.

items.q: What happens after the trip?
items.a: After returning, students will submit reflection assignments, participate in a cultural night presentation at school, and receive academic credits or a certificate. They will also be encouraged to continue their language and cultural learning journey.

items.q: Are there opportunities after the trip?
items.a: Yes, KICC can help arrange post-trip opportunities such as internships in education, cultural exchange, non-profit organizations, or creative industries; Mandarin language programs; and extended exchange projects with local schools or communities.

items.q: What is KICC's mission?
items.a: KICC is dedicated to promoting Mandarin learning and international educational exchanges, arranging Chinese cultural exploration activities (such as calligraphy, tea ceremonies, and traditional crafts), and building long-term bridges between students and Asian cultures to prepare youth to become global citizens.
